title: Make the built-in-profile case in the LCLI-730 gate tests actually reach the detector (round-2 review finding)
description:
Filed from the Stage 1 round-2 review of opum-ai/lore-cli#604 (LCLI-730), which APPROVED the change and raised this as its one non-blocking finding. It is a defect in the TEST, not in the shipped warning.

THE FINDING, as measured. The runCheck case "WITH --strict: a 0.1 BUNDLE on the BUILT-IN profile PASSES" (test/check-task-status-enum.test.ts, near line 371) calls writeIndex("0.1") and writes NO .lore/profile.toml. So activeProfilePath(options.root) is undefined, the caller passes no findings, and taskStatusEnumInheritedFindings is never reached. That is the same flaw as the older built-in case this one was added to shore up: the case cannot fail for any reason connected to this rule.

WORSE, IT OVERCLAIMS, and the comment is the part to fix first. Its comment says the case "exercises the resolved-version path instead of the legacy-missing default", which reads as though the detector ran and consulted a resolved bundle version. It does not run at all. The case still shows something true and worth keeping - lore check --strict exits 0 on the built-in profile, which is a real user path - so it should be RELABELLED to say exactly that and nothing more. Do not delete it.

THE OPTIONAL HALF. Add a case that does reach the detector with a built-in-EQUIVALENT profile file - a .lore/profile.toml whose base status is an open optional string and whose task-coupled type therefore cannot warn - so the built-in-equivalence path is covered by a test that can actually fail. If that proves awkward, the relabel alone closes the finding; say which arm you took.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. The shipped rule is correct and was verified: the round-2 review traced the detector and the per-bundle validation to the same profileForBundle(profile, bundle.state), off one resolveBundleState value, so the two cannot disagree, and the dedupe is by type and attributed to the profile file. Nothing in src/ needs to change for this task.

SEQUENCING. Neither LCLI-729 (src/core/decision-ref.ts) nor LCLI-731 (src/core/agent-context.ts) touches test/check-task-status-enum.test.ts, so this does not fold into either and stands alone. It is small: a comment relabel, plus a test case if it fits.
